name: Aluette
summary: Four-player partnership trick-taking game with Spanish-suited cards where suits are irrelevant and partners may signal.
rules_text: Four players in fixed partnerships opposite each other use a 48-card Spanish pack. Card ranks are fixed: 3 of Coins (monsieur), 3 of Cups (madame), 2 of Coins, 2 of Cups, 9 of Cups, 9 of Coins, 2 of Batons, 2 of Swords, then four Aces, four Kings, four Knights, four Jacks, two Nines, four 8s, 7s, 6s, 5s, 4s, two 3s. Dealer gives 9 cards each in threes, leaving 12. If all agree, left of dealer and dealer each get 6 extra cards and discard 6 face down; otherwise leftover is dead. Left of dealer leads. Each player plays one card; highest wins trick, ties spoil trick with no winner and same leader leads. Nine tricks. Player with most tricks wins 1 point for his team, tie broken by who first reached that count. Five deals make a match. Winning last consecutive tricks having won none before scores 2 (mordienne). Surrender may be offered.
rating_reason: Team trick-taking with signals and bluffing, fits talk and roles.
